newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Lack of foreign investment hampering Yugo economy.
newsitem.headline: Lack of foreign investment hampering Yugo economy.

text.p: Yugoslavia's economy failed to meet its growth targets in the first quarter of 1997 because of lack of financial support from abroad, Tanjug news agency quoted the Information Ministry as saying late on Tuesday.
While acknowledging that the economy fell short of gross domestic product, export and industrial output targets, the Ministry drew attention to the country's price and currency stability.
But it said the absence of foreign financial support, combined with a lack of hard currency and the severe illiquidity of local companies and banks, would continue to hamper output and foreign trade.
Targets for 1997 as a whole are 13 percent average GDP growth, 47 percent export growth and 14 percent industrial output growth.

The ministry statement -- issued after Yugoslav Prime Minister Radoje Kontic met Serbian and Montenegrin government officials -- said it was vital to intensify implementation of the government's 1997 economic policy. The first step would be to determine a consolidated balance of public spending for the entire country.
"Future activity should concentrate on resolving the problem of public spending," the statement said.

The economy was not strong enough to generate sufficient taxes to satisfy the needs of public spending, it added, emphasising that the focus of future government action should shift from monetary to fiscal policy in pursuing economic stabilisation.
This implied tackling the issue of the underground or grey economy.
"Solutions...should be sought in economic measures, but more control and inspection is also needed to resolve the problem of the grey economy," the statement said.
"Another very important task is to intensify efforts for Federal Republic of Yugoslavia to return to international financial and trade organisations," it added.
The government also said it would devote efforts to privatisation and liberalisation.
